title: RTL Verification for Secure Speculation Using Contract Shadow Logic
problem: Speculative execution attacks exploit microarchitectural side channels in out-of-order processors, but rigorous formal verification of hardware RTL designs against speculative security contracts has been lacking, leaving unknown vulnerabilities despite proposed mitigations.
motivation: New speculative execution attacks continue to emerge because hardware mitigations are designed without formal, RTL-level proof of security, making a formal verification framework for processor designs against speculation contracts urgently needed.
method: Contract Shadow Logic introduces a formal RTL verification methodology that augments a processor's RTL with shadow logic encoding speculative execution contracts (defining what information a processor's speculative state may leak). The shadow logic tracks information flow through speculative pipelines at the RTL level, and model checking or equivalence checking is used to verify that no execution trace violates the contract, providing machine-checked security guarantees for the hardware design.
key_novelty: Attaching contract-encoding shadow logic directly to processor RTL enables automated, formal verification of speculative execution security properties at the implementation level.
contributions: The Contract Shadow Logic framework for RTL-level formal verification of speculative execution security
A methodology for encoding speculative security contracts as shadow logic attached to processor RTL
Formal verification of security properties against speculative execution attacks directly on hardware designs
Identification of vulnerabilities or confirmation of security for concrete RTL processor designs

metrics.other: formal security verification coverage (specific numbers not in abstract)

baselines: existing software and hardware mitigations for speculative execution attacks
limitations: Scalability of formal verification to full out-of-order processor designs with all speculative features is not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Formal RTL verification of speculative execution security
